 Cam Skattebo rushed 18 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders, adding 44 yards on three receptions.
 Skattebo immediately returned to a workhorse role following the shortcomings of Devin Singletary in Week 10, the latter of whom saw but one opportunity to the 22 of Skattebo. The Skatt-man bookended halftime with a score from one yard out on the team’s final possession of the first half and a score from 13 yards out on the team’s first possession of the second half, earning two backflips in the process. The second-year back also escaped down the sideline for a 34-yard reception in the first quarter to pad his counting stats. Despite the resurgence in workload, Skattebo will be a borderline FLEX option in a difficult matchup against the pass-funnel Jaguars in Week 11. 
 -  Mark Garcia

 “They were certainly big game hunting,” Raanan said. Though the thought of the Falcons parting ways with the centerpiece of their offense sounds ridiculous, it’s clear John Harbaugh and the Giants see themselves as a postseason team that won’t be content with a playoff berth. The inquiry on Bijan speaks to the Giants’ ongoing skepticism of Cam Skattebo as a true lead back. The team has done everything they can to prevent Skattebo from taking on a big backfield workload. In Week 10 against the Commanders, with a flurry of backfield injuries and Devin Singletary coming off one of the worst running back performances in NFL history, the Giants might have no choice but to feed Skattebo, who should be started in all 12-team leagues.

 Ravens head coach Jesse Minter released a statement saying Lamar Jackson (thumb) will be out for the next 6-10 weeks.
 On the short end of this timeline, Jackson could return in Week 16 against the Browns. On the long end, Jackson would be looking at returning around the Wild Card or Divisional Round of the playoffs if the Ravens make the postseason. This timeline closely aligns with the 6-9 week absence NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported earlier in the week. If this isn’t a season-ender for Lamar, it will be close, and how the Ravens perform over the next several weeks with Jacoby Brissett under center will likely determine whether the Ravens dress him for the final few weeks of the season, even if he is ready to go. Minter said that Jackson is “doing well” after suffering his injury in Week 8 against the Bills, which is encouraging, but we’re a long way from knowing if a return for Jackson is truly in the cards. The 4-5 Ravens have lost their last four games but hope to turn things around on Monday night when they play host to the Chargers.
 -  Zachary Krueger

 Falcons signed CB C.J. Henderson to a two-year extension.
 The former 2020 first-rounder can earn up to $20 million on his new deal, per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, with $11 million being guaranteed. Henderson was drafted No. 9 overall by the Jaguars in 2020, but has since bounced around to the Panthers, Texans, and Steelers, and was actually cut by the Falcons in August 2025 during final roster cutdowns after camp. Since then, Henderson has played his way not only onto the 53-man roster, but into a starting role. He has started six of the eight games he has appeared in for Atlanta this season, totaling 41 tackles, nine pass breakups, and one fumble recovery while earning a PFF coverage grade of 65.3. Playing almost exclusively on the outside, he has allowed opposing receivers to go for 252 yards and three touchdowns on 44 targets.

 Malik Nabers caught 5-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders.
 Nabers was clearly not a point of emphasis in a game expected to carry significant weather impacts. Despite the weather subsiding in the second half, McCarthy remained fixed on Isaiah Likely, feeding the veteran tight end 11 targets. The matchup also played a role in the game plan, with the Commanders missing numerous key linebackers while blitzing at an above average rate. Nabers is in a good spot to bounce back against the Jaguars in Week 11, where he’ll return to WR1 status in fantasy circles.

 Malachi Fields caught 3-of-4 targets for 62 yards in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders.
 The New York wide receivers were clearly limited by a game plan to feature tight end Isaiah Likely, with the starting trio of Malik Nabers, Fields, and Darnell Mooney combining for just 10 receptions, one more than the nine of Likely. Even so, Fields continued to demonstrate a strong connection with quarterback J.J. McCarthy as the rookie finished second on the team in receiving despite seeing only four targets. The highlight of the game came in the second half when McCarthy threaded a ball over one defender and underneath two more down the left sideline for a 25-yard gain to Fields. Although his weekly volume likely won’t be vast enough to return consistent fantasy production without an injury to Nabers or Likely, Fields continues to show the growth dynasty managers were hoping for.
 -  Mark Garcia

 J.J. McCarthy completed 23-of-36 passes for 293 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Giants’ 24-21, Week 10 loss to the Commanders, adding 34 yards on six carries. 
 McCarthy appeared to be in complete control throughout before a game-sealing interception with under a minute to play in a three-point game. He demonstrated plus pocket presence and made numerous dime-worthy throws, the most impressive of which was a 25-yard dart to rookie Malachi Fields that was put in the only place where Fields could come down with the ball, over one defender and underneath two more down the left sideline. McCarthy leaned heavily on Isaiah Likely, feeding the veteran tight end 11 targets in what appeared to be a matchup-based game plan in the face of an aggressive pass rush. The Giants fall to 5-3-1 with the loss and pass the first tie-breaker to the Commanders after the two teams’ tie earlier this season. The Giants get a difficult matchup against arguably the most well-rounded roster in the AFC when they host the Jaguars in Week 11, where McCarthy falls to a mid-range QB2 in fantasy circles.
 -  Mark Garcia

 Treylon Burks caught 2-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
 Burks fought through clear discomfort after coming into the game listed questionable following a Wednesday downgrade on the practice report, catching two early passes for 27 yards before succumbing to the inside-funnel nature of the New York defense. Quarterback Jayden Daniels directed 22 of his 33 pass attempts to the trio of Stefon Diggs, Chig Okonkwo, and Ben Sinnott over the middle of the field. Burks’ situation is unlikely to improve in Week 11 with lockdown perimeter corner DJ Turner on deck.

 Ben Sinnott caught all four targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
 Sinnott entered the game with just one reception this season while playing as the primary blocking tight end alongside Chig Okonkwo. Okonkwo departed in the second quarter with a back injury and returned to start the second half, with the time off the field paving the way for Sinnott to triple his year-to-date reception total and score his first touchdown of the season. He would add one reception in the second half to push his total to four. The touchdown reception also came with a bit of intrigue as the pass appeared to be targeting Stefon Diggs in the end zone. Sinnott was on a crossing route at the goal line and happened to cross paths at the perfect time. He will not be fantasy viable for as long as Okonkwo remains healthy.
